problem_motivation.content: The need for structural materials that can withstand severe irradiation environments in next-generation nuclear reactors.
problem_motivation.evidence_span: Searching for structural materials with excellent irradiation tolerance is crucial for developing the next generation nuclear reactors.

prior_approach.content: Previous studies established that high configurational entropy stabilizes solid solutions in equiatomic multi-element HEAs and that only true single-phase solid solutions possess high configurational entropy.
prior_approach.evidence_span: It is well known that the high configurational entropies may stabilize solid solutions in equiatomic, multi-element HEAs. Many attractive properties of HEAs are attributed to the effects induced by the structure of multi-element solid solution, such as large lattice distortion. F. Otto et al. [19] studied the microstructures of six equiatomic quinary alloys with analogous compositions and found that only one of the six alloys formed a single phase solid solution.

prior_approach.content: Prior literature suggests that precipitation in concentrated alloys with three or more principal elements requires model simplification via assumption due to lack of direct investigation.
prior_approach.evidence_span: Since there is no theoretical and experimental investigation about the precipitation behavior in concentrated alloys with principal elements n ≥ 3, it requires such assumption to simplify the model in order to interpret and compare the current experiment results.

prior_approach.content: Previous studies have shown that in Fe-Cr model and engineering materials with Cr concentrations above 10 at.%, ion irradiation can induce or enhance precipitation through homogeneous nucleation.
prior_approach.evidence_span: In many Fe-Cr model and engineering materials with Cr concentrations above 10 at.%, ion irradiation can also induce or enhance the precipitation through homogeneous nucleation mechanism.

prior_approach.content: Prior research by K.-Y. Tsai et al. proposed that lattice potential energy fluctuation in ideal-solution-like HEAs causes atomic traps, leading to high activation energies and low diffusion mobilities.
prior_approach.evidence_span: K.-Y. Tsai et al. [21] studied the sluggish diffusion in an ideal-solution-like Co-Cr-Fe-Mn-Ni HEA and proposed that great fluctuation of lattice potential energy causes the significant atomic traps and blocks, leading to the high activation energies and low diffusion mobilities.

prior_limitation.content: While HEAs have attractive mechanical properties, their structure and composition can change under irradiation, leading to significant performance degradation.
prior_limitation.evidence_span: Despite HEAs exhibiting attractive mechanical properties, their structure and composition may be changed under irradiation, which will significantly degrade their performances.

prior_limitation.content: Prior work indicates that multi-phase alloys with ordered phases or phase separation do not exhibit the characteristic properties of high configurational entropy.
prior_limitation.evidence_span: Furthermore, these experimental results and the related thermodynamic analyses suggest that only the multi-element solid solutions, such as CoCrFeMnNi, have the true high configurational entropies, while for the multi-phase alloys exhibiting ordered phases or in which some kind of phase separation occurs, the configurational entropy, in fact, is not high.

causal_claim.content: The distinct growth of precipitates in A2 phases is attributed to coalescence.
causal_claim.evidence_span: The precipitates in the A2 phases of Al 1.5 CoCrFeNi exhibit a distinct growth with increasing fluence, which is mainly due to the precipitate coalescence

causal_claim.content: High configurational entropy reduces the thermodynamic driving force for precipitation.
causal_claim.evidence_span: In contrast, the configurational entropy of single phase HEA Al 0.1 CoCrFeNi is much higher, which competes with the positive mixing enthalpy in the ion irradiation and reduces the thermodynamic driving force for precipitation.

causal_claim.content: The great structure stability of single phase HEA under ion irradiation is caused by high configurational entropy and low atomic mobility.
causal_claim.evidence_span: As discussed above, the great structure stability of single phase HEA Al 0.1 CoCrFeNi under ion irradiation is attributed to the high configurational entropy and low atomic mobility, which reduces the thermodynamic driving force and kinetically restrains the formation of precipitate, respectively.

causal_claim.content: The formation of ordered phases and phase separation in multiphase HEAs reduces their configurational entropies, causing them to behave like conventional alloys.
causal_claim.evidence_span: For multiphase HEAs, the formation of ordered phases and phase separation reduce their configurational entropies, resulting in that they behave like conventional binary and ternary alloys under irradiation.

mechanism_principle.content: The stability of the single-phase HEA against precipitation is attributed to high configurational entropy reducing thermodynamic driving force and low atomic diffusion kinetically restraining precipitate formation.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: the excellent structural stability against precipitation of Al 0.1 CoCrFeNi is attributed to the high configurational entropy and low atomic diffusion, which reduces the thermodynamic driving force and kinetically restrains the formation of precipitate, respectively.

mechanism_principle.content: Brighter HAADF contrast in precipitates indicates higher heavy element concentration due to Z^2 dependence.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: Compared with matrix, all of these precipitates exhibit a brighter contrast. This suggests that precipitates contain a higher concentration of heavy elements, as compared with matrix, since the intensity in the HAADF image is approximately proportional to Z 2 [18]

hypothesis_statement.content: The study proposes to investigate how microstructure and chemical composition dependences influence the irradiation tolerances of HEAs.
hypothesis_statement.evidence_span: The aim of current study is to investigate the structural stability of HEAs under ion irradiation and explore the microstructure and chemical composition dependences of irradiation tolerances of HEAs.

hypothesis_statement.content: Chemical composition is a more significant factor than crystal structure in determining precipitation behavior.
hypothesis_statement.evidence_span: The precipitates in the A2 phases of Al 1.5 CoCrFeNi have the largest size and the average precipitate sizes in the Cr, Fe-enriched fcc and A2 phases are obviously larger than those in the Al, Ni-enriched B2 phases for both HEAs, suggesting chemical composition plays a more important role in the precipitation behavior than structure in current study.

evidence_result.content: The single phase Al0.1 CoCrFeNi alloy shows structural stability with no precipitation observed under irradiation.
evidence_result.evidence_span: The single phase solid solution, Al 0.1 CoCrFeNi alloy, exhibits a great structural stability against ion irradiation, where precipitation was not observed in TEM characterization even at the highest fluence.

evidence_result.content: Irradiation induces numerous precipitates in multiphase Al0.75 and Al1.5 CoCrFeNi alloys.
evidence_result.evidence_span: In contrast, numerous precipitates can be observed in the irradiated multiphase Al x CoCrFeNi ( x = 0.75 and 1.5) HEAs.

evidence_result.content: Precipitate sizes in A2 phases grow significantly with fluence, while B2 phase precipitates reach saturation.
evidence_result.evidence_span: The precipitates in the A2 phases of Al 1.5 CoCrFeNi exhibit a distinct growth with increasing fluence, which is mainly due to the precipitate coalescence, as shown in Fig. 3(f) . In contrast, the growth of precipitates in the B2 phases is slow, indicating the precipitate sizes approach a saturation value.

evidence_result.content: At fluences below 5 × 10^15 cm^-2, no precipitates are detectable in TEM images.
evidence_result.evidence_span: The inset in Fig. 5 shows the precipitate sizes at 5 × 10 15 cm −2 and 1 × 10 16 cm −2 ; below 5 × 10 15 cm −2 no precipitate can be observed in HAADF or BF images.

evidence_result.content: The lack of observed precipitates in Al0.1 CoCrFeNi may be due to high stability or undetectable size/composition differences.
evidence_result.evidence_span: No precipitate was observed in as-irradiated Al 0.1 CoCrFeNi, indicating high phase stability or else any precipitate size or the composition difference between precipitates and matrix is too small to be detectable by TEM measurements.

constraint.content: The analysis of irradiation effects is limited to the region within 100 nm depth where electron-transparent conditions for high-resolution observation are met.
constraint.evidence_span: Therefore, the irradiation doses are taken as the average dpa within the depth of 100 nm.

constraint.content: TEM foil preparation and subsequent irradiation were restricted to room temperature conditions.
constraint.evidence_span: using 3 MeV Au ions at room temperature

contradiction.content: The current study did not observe irradiation-induced voids or segregation phenomena that were reported in recent studies at elevated temperatures, indicating a discrepancy in irradiation responses between room and high temperatures.
contradiction.evidence_span: It should be noted that recently, K. Jin et al. [40] observed the irradiation-induced voids and its related volume swelling in various multi-component alloys at 500 °C and N.A.P. Kiran Kumar et al. [41] found the irradiation-induced segregation in grain boundaries in FeNiMnCr HEA irradiated at high temperatures. These experimental phenomena are not observed in current study, indicating the irradiation responses of HEA at high temperatures are drastically different from that of room temperature.
